_note: Playoff series model and Cup simulation. Fitted on 165 playoff series 2013-14..2024-25 (excl. 2019-20 bubble): P(team A wins series) = logistic(alpha * (b_power * power-rating difference + b_elite * difference in elite skaters counted up to 2)). Power rating = end-of-season power formula (goals/game); elite = top-12 F and top-6 D by ice time with talent >= 90th percentile at the position. v1.2.0: counting only the first two elite skaters improved leave-one-season-out log-loss from 0.6595 to 0.6468; the full Cup simulation scored the same as the linear version (within simulation noise), alpha 0.7 kept. Experiments: calibration/experiments/cup_odds_backtest_*.

series_backtest.note: Leave-one-season-out over 165 series. prob_score = % improvement in log-loss over a coin flip.

stage_skill.note: Backtest of the full simulation from about 4 and 14 games played, 8 seasons: improvement in log-loss over giving every team equal odds (alpha 0.7, elite counted up to 2).

cup_winners.note: Every Cup winner 2013-14..2024-25 (excl. 2019-20) had at least 2 elite (top-10%) skaters; 7 of 11 had 0 or 1 superstar (top 2%).

favorites: Each season's model favorite (avg ~13% Cup) won 0 of 8 Cups in the backtest (about 1 expected), so treat Cup odds as low-confidence.
